steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Seems we've come up empty handed.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The room shows little sign of recent human activity. His usual household furniture, such as the rocking chair, coffee maker, and shooting target are all covered with dust...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The terminal shows no communication records or abnormal messages. There is no opportunity to produce any additional evidence for now.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Preliminary deduction: Pope Yvangelista XI has been missing for roughly two weeks.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I only met His Holiness once, and already mentally prepared myself, but to know something really has happened to him...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia, explain.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You seem to have a theory as to where His Holiness has gone.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We meet again, 'Grandpa with the Lateran Candy'.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The Curia's joint trial has already concluded, with your signature on the verdict. The condemned shouldn't be having a private meeting with the Pope, though.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: So, what is your decision?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So straightforward? I imagined you'd say something like 'I was just taking my post-dessert walk and accidentally bumped into you'.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As for whether I'm willing to become a so-called 'Saint', I believe we had a thorough discussion on the topic when I was at Rhodes Island—

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We certainly did.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I'm quite fond of that landship myself. A pity our meeting was so short. I still remember that sunset, when you performed a not-so 'Lateran' piece...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I also remember you were hoping for me to provide more evidence.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Do you still remember my words, child? 'That every light we know will one day be extinguished.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hah, it's etched into my mind. It's an interesting expression after all.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: That day will soon come... of course, it is just a hunch.
The Pope points to his own halo.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It's been sending me a lot of warnings lately, but refuses to respond to any of my questions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What does that mean?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: To put it another way, our glorious Law is suddenly no longer interpretable.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I only know how to play the cello, Your Holiness.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Of course, of course. Interpreting holy scripture is the Pope's job.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Trouble has popped up at work, and I have to figure out how to solve it somehow.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So, what do you need me to do?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Stay vigilant... I'm not sure what exactly will happen, so this is the only thing I can say.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: If the Holy City's lights do go out, then trust in your ideal 'understanding', your ideal 'emotion', the kind of unreserved, pure, and honest 'communication' that you seek.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: An Alienus like you will then perhaps become a panacea, or a poison... but regardless, you will turn things around.

spans.text: An Alienus like you will then perhaps become a panacea, or a poison... but regardless, you

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It sounds as if I have no reason to refuse you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Though I'm not the only Alienus Laterano has.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Indeed, I was just about to contact the other Saints.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Though I pray we still have the time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So that is why you began suspecting your surroundings so early.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Not the whole reason, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: One's inner main theme may stay the same, but it's hard for me to miss those supplementary and missing segments, all blended together too seamlessly. Sister Hildegard is a good example.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What concerns me more though, is that the incident happened before His Holiness managed to find you.

spans.text: What concerns me more though, is that the incident happened
His Holiness managed to find you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The situation is too complicated. All of Laterano has fallen into an unfathomable calamity on a scale near to what we experienced in the Witch King's Pavillon.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We require support.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fortunately, I have my cello with me.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister?
There is no answer.
Vannini walks around the workshop but fails to find her master. She spots a bottle of eye drops on the workbench, uncapped.

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: Vani! About time!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: H-Huh?

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: A gun-knight came by earlier and took Paganini away.

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: Before he left, the gun-knight told me to tell you to hurry over to the Curia to assist their investigation.

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: Vani, are you two in some sort of trouble?

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: Either way, you'd better get to the Curia. The gun-knight wasn't in the best of moods.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister...
It must be because of her and El. But no matter, she thinks, her master should not get caught up in this.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Wait, these are...
Some bullet casings are scattered on the workbench, as if they were casually left by a careless gunsmith.
Vannini puts on her gloves and begins collecting them as she usually does. But suddenly she feels as if she recognizes these casings, like they're old friends.
The shells are smooth to the touch—even the etchings have been rubbed flat—how many times have they been handled? What kind of bullet casings would receive such care, and in whose hands?
Vannini takes off her gloves. She touches a casing, the metal still slightly warm.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Pag...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Deus meus! Lord Almighty! You scared the glasses off me!

spans.text: Lord Almighty! You scared the glasses off me!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Are you finally going to say something? You're already four, you know? Any Sankta your age should be speaking, with a bright halo over their head!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Alright, I was hallucinating. You still can't talk.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I would have left this rotten place long ago if I hadn't picked you up by chance. Just thinking about having to live in the same city as that damned Patrizion makes me sick.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: How many hospitals and churches have we been to? Huh? And still, no one has any idea if you were just born like this, or if your 'Lord' has a problem with you...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: It's been three years. You have no halo, and neither do I, so of course I have no clue what's going on in your head. Seems like I've gotten used to my 'little mute' here, and even I myself am growing quieter day by day.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Whatever. You haven't run off in the middle of the night, so I'll just assume you like it here.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: That's enough from me, considering how responsive you are. If you ever want to communicate with me, you'll have to figure out a way yourself.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Vani, let go!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Why the sudden hugging and crying and laughing? Did I flip a switch somewhere...?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You don't usually respond to anything I say. Are you trying to make up for all these years at once?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Also, what's with the sudden light over your head? Those doctors and clerics treating you the past three years couldn't do a thing...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: But you picked a gun with that Lemuel kid and now you're fine?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Gah, still can't speak, hm? Don't you Sankta sprout halos from your first word? Did your halo come out early because it got impatient?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Grabs her master's hand and nods vigorously)

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I'm no Sankta, so I don't get how you communicated with that kid through the guardian gun, or how much it mattered to you...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: In any case, now I know you can understand me perfectly, and that's enough for me.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Gripping her master's face feathers)

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Okay, okay, okay! That hurts!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: If you're willing to listen, I can teach you a less violent way to communicate.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Sit here—and stay! Look at these bullet casings. Here, I'll teach you—

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: S-Since when... am I able to talk? I shouldn't...
To little Vannini, 'understanding' and 'expression' were a pair of rusty doors blocking her from communicating.
She lived with the garrulous and eccentric Liberi for three years, unable to figure out when he was happy or angry, unable to express her own annoyance or adoration.
She never thought a Sankta with both fiery hair and personality would blast a hole into her sealed-off heart without the need for words.

Later, her master pieced small bullet casings together and, word by word, taught her a whole new language. Even after she finally learned some simple phrases, they still used the shells to communicate.

But today she no longer remembers when exactly she did finally manage to grasp the most complex of sentences, let alone how many times she nonchalantly tossed the shells left by her master into the trash.
She dares not imagine his perplexed face as he rubbed the shells they used for more than a decade, wondering why his student no longer cherishes this special language from the depths of her memory.
Through tearful eyes, she realizes once more what those casings mean—it's a warning!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: No... Magister!

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: Oh, Vani. I just remembered something that was bothering me.

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: When the gun-knight took Paganini away, it didn't look like they were heading for the Curia.

steps.name: Sankta Neighbor
steps.text: I'd say they were going... toward the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Cardinal Lemuen. Forgive for my tardiness, I was just sorting out the gunsmithy handover documents. There's just so much—

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Why are you here?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Cardinal Aide Amos. Have a seat.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Easy now. Just passing on the Curia's newest orders.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: What kind of orders require your presence—

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The Curia has decided to suspend all of Cardinal Lemuen's work, and you shall serve as an acting cardinal of the Seventh Tribunal until her work review is complete.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Wh-What?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You heard me.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The Seventh Tribunal was raided by unknown forces recently, and the suspect Lemuel, who attempted to disrupt the Summit of Nations, managed to escape during the chaos.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Cardinal Lemuen made contact with the suspect, but released her without authorization.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: After further investigation, it was discovered she acted similarly during the Pagus Stevonus explosion and the attack on the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Cardinal Lemuen has engaged in severe violations of the Seventh Tribunal's code of conduct, as well as the Law...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: But, why me?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We wouldn't have captured the suspect without the crucial evidence you provided, and perhaps the Nativity would've been sabotaged.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Amos, you've spent more than a decade in the Seventh Tribunal, correct?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Two more months, and it will be exactly fourteen years.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You're the oldest functionary here, and are familiar with the Seventh Tribunal's business. Does that not make you the most suitable candidate?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It may have been an absence of opportunity, rather than a personal lack of ability, that has prevented you from playing a more important role.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Be more confident in yourself, boy!

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Reverend Patrizion, I've always felt you did not like me much...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I still remember the first time Aurela and I went to visit you. It was not you, but Fiammetta, who had just came home from school, welcomed us.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I mean, I don't like you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Aurela was my best student, exceptionally talented in armored combat and firearms. But she had too much of a character, and an extreme way of doing things...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: While you, on the opposite, were too weak... And yet, these are your own choices.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I'll just say this again, I wasn't home that day because my armor broke and needed fixing!

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Besides, if we're going to make it personal between us, you're the one who's holding a deeper grudge, right? I personally expelled Aurela from Laterano, after all.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: When it comes to that... I only blame myself.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: You're right. I'm too weak, and have nothing to my name.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I couldn't help Aurela defuse her anger, even though I was right there with her. And so, she hurt the shackled Sarkaz in the abbey, and ultimately leveled her gun at her own people.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: And after she made that terrible mistake, I...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I didn't even manage to see her one last time, Reverend Patrizion...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I... I really can't do anything...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Then think on what you can still do right now.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Now?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The Summit of Nations is still ongoing, and the Seventh Tribunal has lots of business on hand. You will be temporarily created cardinal, as the Curia has decided.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Handshake review complete. You now have access to cardinal privileges and permissions.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: W-Wait, so fast? I... I still haven't...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Cardinal Amos, in the face of calamity, Laterano must strive for efficiency.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: So, there will be no welcome tea and cake for you.
With the gun-knight gone, Amos pulls out a chair. He opens his terminal, and his privileges have indeed already been updated, as Patrizion said.
Everything happened so fast he needs some time to adjust... and he suddenly realizes something.
He taps on the file explorer, and scrolls all the way down, finally arriving at his target at the bottom.
He opens the document, his finger pausing on a signature confirmation page.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Aurela, I finally...
Newly created Cardinal Amos sees a smile on his face reflected on the terminal screen.
It is a little ridiculous, he thinks.

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: Uh... th-this is...

steps.name: Sankta B
steps.text: It's Laterano. We're finally back.

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: No, something's off... those strangely colored shadows... look at their shapes!

steps.name: Sankta B
steps.text: They're projecting... the Shrine of Nurtury?

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: What's going on? Has Laterano changed, or do we have brain damage?

steps.name: Sankta B
steps.text: Watch out! Behind you!

steps.name: Enlightened Creature
steps.text: (Praying)

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: A creature with a halo? What?!

steps.name: Sankta B
steps.text: There's more and more of them! Wait, stay back, I don't need an extra halo on me—

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: Nice shot! They don't dodge bullets. We should be fine.

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: Why do you look so dazed? Let's clear a way out... what's wrong?

steps.name: Sankta A
steps.text: You're... fallen?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Our awakenings may have influenced others to wake up as well. But there are also more of these halo-sporting creatures.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Those creatures dragged the awakened into the strangely-colored projections, and then vanished together.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They did not even manage to retaliate. And the Sankta who shot at those creatures... have fallen?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, I'm afraid my joke from before was no joke at all. These things are... considered Sankta, and thus our people?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How strange and chaotic their hearts sound... what should I listen for within the mess? What should I share with them?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Ah... they can't feel our emotions either, and are anxious over it. They desperately want to share theirs, but they can only resort to brute force.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Like an infant yet to grow a halo—no matter what they want to express, they can only cry and grab at their parents' sleeves... Yes, they are our people, just too immature.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Immature, but powerful.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Law grants an infant a halo when it speaks its first word because language represents rationality's awakening.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And rationality refers to a Sankta finally gaining the capacity to be conscientious of both their people and the Law.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why would the Law deem a pack of nonsentient creatures as 'Sankta', and also compel them to use brute force to intervene in their people's fates?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Anomalies only continue to multiply. Currently, the only individual we may cooperate with is the Doctor. Being present already, the Doctor must know something about the current situation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia, are you certain the Doctor remembers the sound of your strings?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The Doctor was almost present at every of my few performances on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A pity the Doctor was never my intended audience, but I ought to be glad the Doctor seemed to have been listening carefully every single time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Only your first sentence contained actual information, Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Haha. Sure.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Well then, Fede. I will guide the Doctor with my cello.
A sudden notification beep interrupts the two.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Here and now, of all times...?
Federico checks his communicator.
Hello...? Can... you hear... me?
Aurela... former citizen ID... LC0073458.
A group of errari Sankta and war refugees... currently north of the Lateran City... three kilometers out...
Requesting permission to enter the city.
